projects.name: Hollowstone
projects.tagline: An original block-building sandbox, built from scratch in the browser.
projects.summary: Dig, build and explore an endless voxel world, with its own blocks, art, creatures and a signature mechanic.
description: Hollowstone is an open-world block-building sandbox that runs right in your browser. The world is infinite and made of blocks: dig down, build up, and explore a landscape generated from a seed.

The genre is familiar, but everything inside it is our own: block names, textures, sounds, creatures and at least one mechanic you won't find anywhere else. The project follows a written set of originality rules.
projects.noShots: No playable build yet. The first screenshots will land here once terrain (M1) is on screen.

features.title: Infinite chunked world
features.text: Terrain generated from seeded noise and streamed in around the player.

features.title: Dig and build
features.text: Break and place blocks anywhere, with saves that survive.

features.title: All-original content
features.text: Our own blocks, art, sound and creatures, following the originality rules.

features.title: Runs in the browser
features.text: No install: open the page and play.

projects.name: Xenohold
projects.tagline: Round-based alien survival shooter. Hold the line, buy the doors, survive the hive.
projects.summary: First-person wave survival across 17 arenas, with perks, wall guns, a Mutation Forge, bosses and a full map editor.
description: Xenohold is a round-based first-person survival shooter. Alien creatures pour in from vents every round; you earn points, open buyable doors deeper into the map, buy wall guns and perks, and upgrade your weapons at the Mutation Forge.

There are 17 hand-dressed arenas, from Hesperus City (a 245 m colony capital at night with nine districts) to a lunar base with low gravity and a flooded temple of alien ruins. Each has its own lighting, weather, music, main quest and story told through the rooms, plus readable logs.

It ships with Xenohold Editor, a full map editor with a live 3D view: paint walls and floors, raise and ramp the ground, place props, traps and triggers, script events, set the waves, and test your map instantly.

features.title: 17 arenas
features.text: Each split into named, furnished rooms, with buyable doors, perk machines, a power generator and a main quest.

features.title: 9 creatures and bosses
features.text: Plus a unique creature on every map and three alternate bosses, including the deep-water Drowner.

features.title: Guns, perks and the Forge
features.text: Wall weapons, perk machines and Pack-a-Punch-style upgrades, including chain-lightning electric guns.

features.title: Map editor
features.text: Build your own maps from scratch, with triggers, moving and breakable pieces, waves and spawn points.

features.title: Story in the world
features.text: Readable datapads, remains and barricades tell what happened in each place.

features.title: Built for big fights
features.text: Skinned creature meshes and occlusion culling keep large hordes smooth.

roadmap.title: Maps overhaul: every arena dressed for what it is
Raise, lower and ramp the ground
Triggers, scripted events and per-map waves

projects.name: Xenohold: Godot Edition
projects.tagline: The native Godot 4 rebuild of Xenohold. No browser, straight to your graphics card.
projects.summary: A native rebuild of Xenohold in Godot 4.7, ported map by map from the web version.
description: Xenohold: Godot Edition is a native rebuild of Xenohold in Godot 4.7. It runs directly on your graphics card, with no browser and no launcher window.

Rather than rewriting everything by hand, a custom export pipeline pulls the maps, creatures, guns, textures, music and sound straight out of the web game and bakes them into Godot scenes. That means the web version stays the place where content is authored.
Outpost Kestrel and Bastion 9 are playable now, from the first round to wherever you fall.

features.title: Native performance
features.text: Runs on Godot's renderer with baked lighting, with no browser overhead.

features.title: Export pipeline
features.text: Maps, creatures, weapons, PBR surfaces, music and sound exported straight from the web game.

features.title: Two maps playable
features.text: Outpost Kestrel and Bastion 9, full rounds.

roadmap.title: Editor zones, barrels and placed traps

projects.name: Gunship: Overwatch
projects.tagline: Thermal gunship defence. Tens of thousands of infected. One stadium left to hold.
projects.summary: You're the sensor operator of a gunship circling the last safe zone. Climb 8 weapon ladders, survive three-day campaigns, or fly the A-10.
description: Gunship: Overwatch puts you in the sensor operator's seat of a gunship flying a left-hand orbit over the last safe zone in the city: a stadium. Tens of thousands of infected are walking toward it, and you start with two machine guns.

Every kill earns requisition points. Spend them climbing eight weapon ladders (71 systems, from twin .50s to a lunar strike) and on permanent upgrades to the aircraft. After every wave you pick one of three roguelite perks, and your career carries over to every area of operations.

Each area is a three-day campaign broken up by jobs from the people on the ground, ending in an evacuation flight you have to cover. Or switch seats and fly CAS: hand-fly an A-10 while the AI flies the gunship.

features.title: IR and colour TV sensors
features.text: Thermal and daylight cameras, with palettes and real line-of-fire rules.

features.title: 71 weapon systems
features.text: Eight ladders, each rung unlocked by buying the one below it.

features.title: Roguelite perks
features.text: Pick one of three after every wave for the rest of the sortie.

features.title: Three-day campaigns
features.text: Missions from the ground, night and weather, bosses and a final evacuation.

features.title: Fortify the refuge
features.text: Build fortifications and passive defences around the stadium.

features.title: CAS mode
features.text: Hand-fly the A-10 close-air-support run while the gunship is AI-flown.

projects.name: Hellswarm
projects.tagline: A neon arcade shooter. The hive came back hotter.
projects.summary: Endless formation-shooter waves, Hive Queen bosses, roguelite upgrades and MELTDOWN. Free to play in your browser.
description: Hellswarm is a neon arcade shooter in the spirit of the classic formation shooters. Alien hive waves swoop in, lock into formation and dive at you. It never ends, and it keeps getting hotter.

Chain kills for up to an x8 multiplier, skim bullets to build heat, and fill the bar to trigger MELTDOWN. Every five waves the Hive Queen arrives with three phases of bullet patterns. All the sound and music is synthesized live in the browser.

features.title: Endless waves
features.text: Random modifiers: Hyperspeed, Armored, Barrage, Kamikaze, Gold Rush, Splitters.

features.title: Hive Queen
features.text: A boss every five waves, with three bullet-pattern phases.

features.title: Roguelite upgrades
features.text: Pick one of three after wave 2 and after every boss.

features.title: Chain, graze, MELTDOWN
features.text: Up to x8 multiplier, heat from grazing bullets, and a screen-clearing meltdown.

features.title: Pickups
features.text: Spread, laser, homing missiles, shield, nova bombs and wingman drones.

features.title: Juice
features.text: Bloom, particles, shockwaves, screen shake, hitstop and live-synthesized audio.

projects.name: ID Forge
projects.tagline: A real-time 3D studio for designing fictional ID cards, badges and passes.
projects.summary: Holographic, smoked-glass and paper cards rendered live in three.js, with 448 presets, real QR codes and turntable exports.
description: ID Forge is a three.js studio for designing fictional ID cards, badges and passes, from rough paper IDs to smoked-glass, translucent, holographic cards rendered in real time.

Design in a full flat editor with layers, snapping and guides, then see it on a physically lit 3D card with gloss, holograms and UV ink you can reveal with a blacklight torch. Export beauty shots, turntable videos and print-ready flat sides.
It's built for games, film and TV props, worldbuilding and cosplay. It contains no real government templates, and its machine-readable strips are decorative only.

projects.name: World Manager
projects.tagline: Run a fictional colony world: a living planet, its people, its history and its lore.
projects.summary: A generated planet you can explore and sculpt, character sheets, a codex, dice and an endless timeline. Offline, installable, one file.
description: World Manager is a self-contained web app for running a fictional colony world. It opens on your planet: real generated terrain on a slowly turning globe, with cloud, sunlight and air.

Explore, sculpt and paint the map, and settle it with places, roads, rivers and borders. Track characters with health, stats, afflictions and blessings, inventories, magic and relationships. Keep a codex of lore, quests and session logs, roll dice, and move through an endless timeline counted from Colony Standard year zero.
Everything lives in one HTML file. It works offline and installs like an app.

projects.name: Ghost PiP
projects.tagline: Click-through picture-in-picture for any window on Windows.
projects.summary: Mirror a video, stream or call into a see-through, always-on-top overlay your mouse passes straight through.
description: Ghost PiP mirrors any live window (a YouTube video, a Twitch stream, a Discord call) into a borderless, always-on-top overlay that your mouse passes straight through.
Make it as see-through as you like, trim it to just the part you care about, and keep watching while you play or work underneath it.
Version 2 is a full rewrite in C# and WPF: a single exe with a live-preview window picker, multiple mirrors at once, per-app crop memory, a live crop editor, media controls and per-app volume.

features.title: Click-through overlay
features.text: Always on top and transparent to your mouse, so you keep working underneath.

features.title: Live window gallery
features.text: Pick a window from live previews, with search and keyboard control.

features.title: Many mirrors
features.text: As many as you like, each with its own settings.

features.title: Remembers per app
features.text: Crop, size and position saved for each site or app.

features.title: Media controls
features.text: A mini-player that talks to the mirrored app's media session.

features.title: Per-app volume
features.text: Volume and mute for the mirrored app, plus rebindable hotkeys.

roadmap.title: Multiple mirrors, per-app memory, live crop

projects.name: Pixel Guys
projects.tagline: Two little pixel buddies who live in the corner of your screen.
projects.summary: Weather Guy and Net Guy pop up with a speech bubble when they have something to tell you, even over your games.
description: Pixel Guys are two 32×32 pixel buddies who live in the corner of your Windows screen and pop up with a speech bubble when they have something to tell you, even over your games.

Weather Guy tells you the weather, warns you about storms and dresses for it, with about 200 outfits, holiday costumes and little weather moments: he goes supernova when it's too hot and rows a boat in a downpour.

Net Guy watches your internet. When it drops, lags or gets jittery, he tells you where the problem is: your Wi-Fi, this PC, another device in the house, or your provider. Both are click-through and never steal focus.

gallery.caption: Weather moments: supernova, ice block, boat and more
Net Guy diagnosing a slow connection

features.title: Weather Guy
features.text: Forecasts, storm warnings and air quality, dressed for the weather.

features.title: 200 outfits
features.text: Plus holiday costumes and animated weather moments.

features.title: Net Guy

features.title: Click-through
